newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks steady, low-priced stocks active.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks steady, low-priced stocks active.

text.p: Singapore shares kicked off the morning trade on Friday on a steady to firm note on the back of Wall Street, dealers said.
At 0220 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was up 7.05 to 2,227.41. Market turnover was around 98 million shares with gainers outpacing losers by 169 to 71.

Low-priced shares such as SMB United and Armstrong Industrial hogged the spotlight as retail investors piled in. Switchgear maker SMB United rose Singapore $0.03 to S$0.375 and topped the actives with more than 21 million shares traded.
Precision engineering specialist Armstrong saw about five million shares traded. Malaysian counters were also active, led by finance company MBF Holdings and property-based Berjaya Industrial.
"These are cheap stocks and (most of the Malaysian stocks) are sleeping beauties that were dead for years," said a dealer.
"Once there is interest in these stocks, people take a punt and activity increases," said the dealer, adding that these stocks used to be runners.
Singapore Press foreign led gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$28.40 while IPCO fell US$0.14 to US$2.56.
